name: sdlc-graph-engineering
description: The SDLC as a guarded graph a machine can actually execute — the graph that drives a feature end to end, the viewer that shows a run as it happens, and the method that turns any other process into a graph of its own.

plugins.name: sdlc-graph
plugins.description: The SDLC as a guarded graph, with the milestone loop delegated to a milestone agent per milestone (per worktree under strategy C) whose bundle the orchestrator verifies against git before recording it. A run is one gitignored directory — state, per-milestone journals, and with --trace every state it passed through. Ships a run reviewer that turns a finished run into the evals it should have had, and an advisory onboarding skill that reports which optional tools this session can invoke and what a run does without each. Command-invoked.

plugins.name: sdlc-graph-viewer
plugins.description: The run viewer for sdlc-graph — one zero-dependency page that renders parallel milestone agents, live or as a self-contained snapshot. Reads the run-directory layout: docs/graph-runs/<run-id>/{state.json,journals/}.

plugins.name: sdlc-graph-engineering-install
plugins.description: Installs graph engineering into a project that has none: turns an existing process — skills, a runbook, a CI config, or a description — into a guarded graph with typed nodes, total exit guards, bounded retry loops, a run-state file, a skipped-step ledger, and its own auditor. Domain-agnostic; needs no other plugin installed.
